Enrichment analysis using g:Profiler (gprofiler2)

Source: R/enrichments.R
artmsEnrichProfiler.Rd

This function simplifies the enrichment analysis performed by the excellent tool g:Profiler, using the gost() function of the gprofiler2 package (which replaces the deprecated gProfileR package). An internet connection is required.

Usage

artmsEnrichProfiler(
  x,
  categorySource = c("GO"),
  species,
  background = NA,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

(list, data.frame) List of protein ids. It can be anything: either a list of ids, or you could also send a data.frame and it will find the columns with the IDs. Is not cool? Multiple list can be also sent simultaneously, as for example running: tmp <- split(enrichment$Gene, enrichment$cl_number, drop= TRUE)

categorySource

(vector) Resources providing the terms on which the enrichment will be performed. The resources supported by g:Profiler are:

  • GO (GO:BP, GO:MF, GO:CC): Gene Ontology. GO selects the three of them

  • KEGG: Biological pathways

  • REAC: Biological pathways (Reactome)

  • WP: Biological pathways (WikiPathways)

  • TF: Regulatory motifs in DNA (TRANSFAC TFBS)

  • MIRNA: Regulatory motifs in DNA (miRTarBase microRNAs)

  • CORUM: protein complexes database

  • HP: Human Phenotype Ontology

  • HPA: Protein databases (Human Protein Atlas) OMIM is no longer available in g:Profiler and it is ignored. Electronic GO annotations (IEA) are excluded.

species

(char) Specie code: Organism names are constructed by concatenating the first letter of the name and the family name. Example: human - ’hsapiens’, mouse - ’mmusculus’. Check g:Profiler to find out more about supported species.

background

(vector) gene list to use as background for the enrichment analysis. Default: NA (no custom background: all known genes are used)

verbose

(logical) TRUE (default) shows function messages

Value

(data.frame) The significant enrichment results (zero rows if there are none)

Details

This function calls gprofiler2::gost() with these arguments:

  • ordered_query = FALSE

  • significant = TRUE

  • exclude_iea = TRUE

  • measure_underrepresentation = FALSE

  • evcodes = TRUE (needed to report the intersection column)

  • user_threshold = 0.05

  • correction_method = "g_SCS" (named "analytical" in gProfileR)

  • domain_scope = "known", or "custom" when a background is provided

The column names of the results are kept as in previous versions of artMS (based on gProfileR): query.number, significant, p.value, term.size, query.size, overlap.size, recall, precision, term.id, domain, term.name, intersection. Note that domain now uses the g:Profiler source names (e.g. GO:BP, KEGG, REAC).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# annotate the MSstats results to get the Gene name
data_annotated <- artmsAnnotationUniprot(
                                     x = artms_data_ph_msstats_results,
                                     columnid = "Protein",
                                     species = "human")

# Filter the list of genes with a log2fc > 2
filtered_data <- 
unique(data_annotated$Gene[which(data_annotated$log2FC > 2)])

# And perform enrichment analysis
data_annotated_enrich <- artmsEnrichProfiler(
                                   x = filtered_data,
                                   categorySource = c('KEGG'),
                                   species = "hsapiens",
                                   background = unique(data_annotated$Gene))
} # }
